narr: Two rounds of storms moved across southeast Minnesota on May 19th. The first occurred from late morning through the middle of the afternoon and produced primarily large hail across Mower and Olmsted Counties. The largest reported hail with this activity was ping pong ball sized near Lyle (Mower County), Adams (Mower County), south of Rochester (Olmsted County) and east of Rochester. The second round of storms also produced hail, although not as large as the earlier storms. The largest reported hail in the late afternoon was quarter sized north of Genoa (Olmsted County). A large tree, estimated to be four feet in diameter, was blown down near Whalan (Fillmore County). Flash flooding across eastern Winona County caused several mud slides, washouts and some cars were submerged in water. Winona County declared a state of emergency and the Governor of Minnesota authorized emergency assistance to help with the recovery.
ev: Runoff from heavy rains caused mud slides and washouts to occur in the area around Homer with the debris covering several roads. Some cars were submerged in the flood waters. A state of emergency was declared and the Governor of Minnesota authorized emergency assistance to help with the recovery.
lsr: MUDSLIDES REPORTED ACROSS ROADS IN HOMER.
